edge_cases: E1 (CONFIRMED LIVE) — post-#675 runs carry all four legacy counters at 0 while imported_count is non-zero, so the NAIVE predicate 'collapsed = legacy sums on every row' false-positives on a healthy row. Staging's single run (imported_count 29, all four legacy 0) flags under the naive form and passes under the two-branch form. The header must carry the two-branch disjunction the ticket comment specified: abort only on a row that did legacy work AND whose collapsed values disagree.

E2 — a pre-#675 run that processed nothing has all four legacy counters at 0 and both collapsed counters at 0, so it satisfies both branches. Harmless: it is indistinguishable from a post-#675 row and needs no reconciliation.

E3 — a pre-#675 row that did real work but recorded zero legacy counters would be misclassified into the post-#675 branch and pass unchecked. It cannot exist: the pre-#675 worker dual-wrote both column sets in the same UPDATE, so non-zero collapsed implies non-zero legacy. Stated explicitly in the header so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.

E4 — a local test DB behind head still has the four columns, so the migration-103 suite sees them present and fails. That is the correct loud failure (assertSchemaReady's contract); the assertion message names migration 103 so the fix — pnpm test:db:setup — is obvious from the failure alone.

E5 — production zernio_backfill_runs is empty (0 rows, 0 businesses), so its preflight is trivially satisfied. It is still run and its zero-row result still recorded; a skipped preflight is not a passed preflight.

E6 — migration-100-import-consent.integration.test.ts currently asserts the legacy four are PRESENT (expect(cols).toHaveLength(7)). It goes red the moment the local DB is provisioned past 103, so it must move in the SAME PR as the migration.

E7 — git revert of THIS PR removes the migration file but does not un-drop applied columns. After 103 applies, reverting a pre-#675 epic PR puts the old dual-writing worker against a schema without those columns (42703). The header states 103 as the point where the epic's revert-only backout stops being sufficient.

E8 — ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and can collide with an in-flight backfill. SET lock_timeout = '5s' (099/100/101 precedent) makes that a fast failure rather than a queue behind a long transaction.
